Mangudadatu House of Representatives Batasan Hills, Quezon City Dear Mr. Idris, This pertains to your letter dated November 22, 2016 addressed to Secretary Ismael D. Sueno, seeking the legal Opinion of this Department on your queries quoted as follows: 1. "Why is the age requirement for Governor and Vice-Governor is 23 while the age requirement for Mayor and Vice-Mayor is 23 or 21 depending on whether or not the city or municipality is urbanized? Does it vary depending on the municipality or city and why?" 2. "What is the substantial difference being emphasized when there is discrimination or selection in imposing different age requirements?" Relevant to your queries are the following pertinent provisions of Republic Act No. 71601 which specifically provide: "SEC. 39. Qualifications.- (b) Candidates for the position of governor, vice-governor or member of the sangguniang panZaZawigan, or mayor, vice- mayor or member of the sangguniang panlungsod of highly urbanized cities must be at least twenty-three years of age on election day. 1 The Local Government Code of 1991

(c) Candidates for the position of mayor or—ice mayor of •omponent cities, component cities, or independent municipalities must be at least twenty-one (21) years of age on election day. (d) Candidates for the position of member of the sangguniang pan lungsod or sangguniang bayan must be at least eighteen (18) years of age on election day. The precursors of these provisions are Republic Act No. 66442 and Batas Pambansa Bilang 3373 which were approved on December 28, 1987 and February IO, 1983, respectively. Indeed, according to the above-quoted provisions of Republic Act No. 7160, it seems that there are apparent distinctions as regards the age qualifications depending upon the nature of local elective positions as identified and grouped therein. Anent thereto, please be informed that the Department of the Interior and Local Government is not in the position to give any legal opinion or explanation as to the rationale behind the inclusion of such provisions in the law, particularly prescribing age qualifications of local elective officials as presently contained under Republic Act No. 7160. The imposition of age requirement vis-å-vis local elective positions is a matter of congressional wisdom that is best addressed by that institution of the government either through its journals or other supporting documents serving as repository of their explanations. 2 An Act Reducing the the Minimum Age of the different Elective Local Officials by amending Section Forty-two of Batas Pambansa Blg. Tatlong Daan Tatlumpu't Pito, otherwise known as the Local Government Code: "Section 1. SECTION 1. Section forty-two of Batas Pambansa Blg. Tatlong Daan Tatlumpu't Pito is hereby amended to read as follows: SEC. 42. Qualifications.—(l) An elective local official must be a citizen of the Philippines, a registered voter in the barangay, municipality, city or province where he proposes to be elected, a resident therein for at least one year at the time of the filing of his certificate of candidacy, and able to read and write Filipino, English, or any other local language or dialect. (2) Candidates for the position of governor, vice-governor, or member of the sangguniang panla/awigan must be at least twenty-three years of age on election day. (3) Candidates for the positions Of mayor Or vice-mayor must be at least twenty-one years Of age on election day. (4) Candidates for the positions of member of the Sangguniang panlungsod or member of the sangguniang bayan must be at least eighteen years of age on election day. If elected as a member of the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan, the member is qualified to fill any vacancy in the office of mayor or vice-mayor or may be appointed by the President upon recommendation of the Secretary of Local Governments as mayor or vice-mayor pursuant to Chapter 2, Title Two of this Code: Provided, That said member is at least twenty- one years of age at the time of his succession." 3 An Act Enacting a Local Government Code

Further, it is well-settled by the law and jurisprudence that in statutory -onstruction, whenever the law is clear and unambiguous, there is no room for any other interpretation thereof aside from its plain, simple and unequivocal meaning. However, it bears stressing here is the provision that the enactment of the Local Government Code is founded on the policy of the State that the territorial and political subdivisions of the State shall enjoy genuine and meaningful local autonomy to enable them to attain their fullest development as self-reliant communities and make them more effective partners in the attainment of national goals. Toward this end, the State shall provide for a more responsive and accountable /oca/ government structure instituted through a system of decentralization whereby local government units shall be given more powers, authority, responsibilities and resources.4 Likewise, the establishment in every local government unit an accountab/e, efficient, and dynamic organizationa/ structure is one of the operative principles of decentralization.5 (emphasis ours) Withal, we advise you to refer to the journals of Congress for a more authoritative disquisition of the queries you raised. We hope that we have guided you accordingly. Thank you very much. Very truly yours, ISMAEL D.
